correctness.rationale: All 21 facets from KG(7,2) are explicitly defined. verify.py exhaustively tests the 2,097,151 nonempty vertex subsets and matches the 37,527-face vector. It constructs 18,633 matchings and topologically sorts every one of 218,673 directed Hasse incidences; only one critical vertex and 260 critical 3-faces remain. Forman yields the integral wedge. Two separately implemented exact S7 chain-character formulas match for 15 classes; exact rim-hook characters are orthonormal and the stated rational multiplicities sum to 260. Computations were executed successfully from verify.py in this package. Assumptions, boundary convention, and limitations are explicitly stated. Independent bitset elimination on the original simplicial boundary maps gives mod-two reduced Betti number 260 in degree 3 and zero otherwise; this corroborates but is not the integral proof.

originality.rationale: The identified closest six-point closed-neighborhood computation includes all six-point homotopy and S6 character, but no theorem extending it to the seven-point S7 module. The primary 2018 Kneser family theorem covers open, not closed, neighborhoods (29 versus 260 spheres for seven ground points). Matsushita provides general functorial equivalences but no seven-point calculation. Exact face and character assertions are separately established. Relevant actual indexed queries and full accessible close-source comparisons found no implication covering the result; unindexed equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent computation of the seven-point closed-neighborhood complex or its S7 character may exist.
The full 2023 categorical-product preprint and other unidentified general product-complex results were not exhaustively inspected; their abstract does not state coverage of K2 times J(7,2).
The finite matching is not S7-equivariant; its character is computed separately from the original chain complex, which is legitimate but yields no equivariant homotopy splitting.

value.rationale: The exact homotopy and full equivariant rational homology classify a canonical next Kneser closed-neighborhood complex. Two different S7 Specht types appear twice, breaking multiplicity-freeness of the previously known S6 case. The exact 260-sphere result also sharply contrasts with the known 29-sphere open-neighborhood complex of the same 21-vertex graph. The precise natural invariant is of use in graph Cech and representation-theoretic topology; value does not depend only on reproducibility.
